plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs to zero.
Exit leveraged semiconductor and AI/Software ETFs.
Reduce concentration in QQQI to 20%.
This plan prioritizes capital preservation.

conservative.read: This mode focuses on preserving capital with a target of around 1.5% per month. It significantly reduces risk by cutting leveraged positions and holding more cash. Drawdowns should be minimal.

plan: Trim leveraged ETFs like SOXL and SPAL to low single digits.
Reduce exposure in leveraged semiconductor and AI/Software ETFs.
Manage concentration in QQQI to 25%.
This plan balances risk and growth.
It aims for a moderate return with controlled risk.
A modest cash buffer will be maintained.
balanced.read: This balanced approach targets about 2.5% per month, prioritizing risk management. It reduces leverage and concentration while maintaining exposure to broad indices and quality tech. Drawdowns are expected to be moderate.

plan: Trim QQQI to manage its concentration.
Increase exposure in leveraged AI/Software and Semiconductor ETFs.
Add to leveraged Space ETF.
This plan aims for aggressive growth.
It uses leverage and concentration to maximize potential returns.
Expect higher potential upside and significantly larger drawdowns.
aggressive.read: This aggressive mode targets around 4% per month, aiming for maximum growth. It leans into leveraged ETFs and concentration, accepting higher risk and potential for large drawdowns. Daily rebalancing of leveraged ETFs can impact performance.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs to zero.
Exit leveraged semiconductor, AI/Software, and Space ETFs.
Increase allocation to QQQI for income generation.
This plan prioritizes steady monthly income.
It aims for low drawdowns and reliable distributions.
A cash buffer will be maintained for stability.
income.read: This income-focused mode targets about 1% per month, prioritizing stable monthly distributions over growth. It cuts leverage and high-beta single names, focusing on income-generating ETFs. While aiming for low drawdowns, NAV can still fall in market downturns.
